theme.title: Heat vs Mavericks, twice
theme.subtitle: 2006 and 2011 Finals
theme.recap: Dwyane Wade carried Miami past Dallas in 2006; five years later Dirk Nowitzki's Mavericks took the rematch.

questions.prompt: Down 2–0 in the 2006 Finals, how many points did Dwyane Wade score to win Game 3?
questions.note: 42 with 13 rebounds, rallying Miami from 13 down.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Led by Dwyane Wade's 42 points and 13 rebounds, the Heat rallied from a 13-point deficit

funFacts.text: Gary Payton capped Miami's late comeback with a jumper in the closing seconds.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The momentum-changing comeback was capped by a Gary Payton field goal from just inside the three-point line with 9.3 seconds left.

funFacts.text: Wade also grabbed 13 rebounds in the crucial home victory.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Led by Dwyane Wade's 42 points and 13 rebounds

funFacts.text: Dirk Nowitzki missed a late free throw that could have tied the game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Dirk Nowitzki had a chance to tie the game at the free throw line with 3.4 seconds to go, but missed 1 of 2

questions.prompt: Dwyane Wade was 2006 Finals MVP. What did he average?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Averaging 34.7 points per game in the series

funFacts.text: Miami fought back from a two-game deficit to claim the series, rather than winning from the front.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat overcame a two-games-to-none series deficit to defeat the Mavericks in six games

funFacts.text: Wade scored 36 points in the clinching road victory at Dallas.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Behind Dwyane Wade's 36 points, Miami rallied from a 14-point first-half deficit

funFacts.text: That Finals victory delivered the first NBA championship in Heat franchise history.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: winning their first NBA championship in franchise history

questions.prompt: In Game 4 of the 2006 Finals, Miami held Dallas to how many fourth-quarter points?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Miami held Dallas to just seven points in the fourth quarter

funFacts.text: Miami's defense held Dallas to an unusually low final-quarter total in a blowout that tied the series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Mavericks' fourth quarter was the lowest ever by any team during the NBA Finals.

funFacts.text: Jerry Stackhouse was suspended for the next game after a flagrant foul in this contest.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Jerry Stackhouse committed a flagrant foul that resulted in his suspension for Game 5.

funFacts.text: Shaquille O'Neal grabbed 13 rebounds in that Miami victory.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rebs: Shaquille O'Neal 13

questions.prompt: Dallas won Game 2 of the 2011 Finals after trailing by how many points?
questions.note: 15, the biggest Finals comeback since Boston rallied from 24 down in 2008.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Mavs' 15-point comeback was the biggest in an NBA Finals game since the 24-point comeback

funFacts.text: Dirk finished the comeback with a driving layup using his injured left hand.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Nowitzki then made a driving layup with his injured left hand with 3.6 seconds left.

funFacts.text: Mario Chalmers briefly tied the game on a three-pointer before Dallas took the decisive possession.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: However, Mario Chalmers tied it with a 3 of his own with 24.5 seconds left

funFacts.text: The Mavericks' victory ended a nine-game home playoff winning streak for Miami.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Mavs' win broke the Heat's 9-game home winning streak in the playoffs
